Sister '''Mary de Lellis Gough''' (15 February 1892 – 7 April 1983) was an Irish nun who spent most of her life in the USA.  She is notable for being the earliest known Irish woman to earn a doctorate in mathematics.

== Life ==

She was born in [[Kilmore, County Wexford]], Ireland. Her parents were Ellen Dunne and Walter Gough. She attended the local St John of God's primary school.<ref name="indo"/> She emigrated to Texas in 1909 with a group of young Irish women, and joined the [[Sisters of Charity of the Incarnate Word]], taking vows as Mary de Lellis in 1911.<ref name="auto">[https://www.ams.org/publications/authors/books/postpub/hmath-34-PioneeringWomen.pdf Supplementary Material For Pioneering Women In American Mathematics: The Pre-1940 Phd’s]
by Judy Green And Jeanne Laduke at [https://www.ams.org/publications/authors/books/postpub/hmath-34 AMS]</ref>

== Career ==
While working as a high school teacher, she studied at the [[Catholic University of America]]. She graduated in 1920, earned a master's degree in 1923, and completed her PhD from the same university in 1931.<ref name="auto"/>
Her PhD dissertation was entitled ''On the condition for the existence of triangles in and circumscribed to certain types of the rational quartic curve and having a common side'' and supervised by [[Aubrey E. Landry]].<ref name="auto"/><ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=42761}}</ref>

She taught mathematics at [[University of the Incarnate Word|Incarnate Word College]] from 1920 to 1943.<ref name="auto"/> In 1953, she coined the term "[[Mathematical anxiety|mathephobia]]" based on her observations of her students.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wen |first=Tiffanie |title=The myth of being 'bad' at maths |url=https://www.bbc.com/worklife/article/20200506-how-to-tackle-your-anxiety-about-maths |access-date=2023-05-14 |website=www.bbc.com |language=en}}</ref>

In 1944, she left teaching due to health issues and returned to Texas where she worked as an accountant at a local hospital in Fort Worth. She retired in 1964.<ref name="indo">{{cite web |title=International Women's Day: Wexford nun is the inspiration behind new Phd in SETU |url=https://www.independent.ie/regionals/wexford/news/international-womens-day-wexford-nun-is-the-inspiration-behind-new-phd-in-setu-42370183.html |website=www.independent.ie |access-date=10 March 2023}}</ref>
